text: This logo lasted about one week.
For years, Gap was known for white letters in a navy blue box. Everyone knew it.
In October 2010, a new logo quietly appeared on gap.com.
say: In October, twenty ten, a new logo quietly appeared on gap dot com.

text: Plain black letters, with a tiny blue square in the corner.
Customers hated it. More than a thousand angry comments hit Gap's Facebook page.
Someone even started a fake Twitter account for the logo, just to mock it.
Gap's answer? Asking customers to send in their own design ideas. That made it worse.
About a week in, Gap brought back the blue box and said: we did not go about this in the right way.
Why the anger? People don't read a logo. They recognise it, like a friend's face.
Swap it overnight, and loyal customers feel like something was taken from them.
Redesigning your website or logo? Keep what people recognise, and test it with real customers first.
